messages:
Deploy Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime-service-3 latency spike + memory growth detected. 95th latency > 1200ms, OOM risk on GPU nodes. Triggered by increased streaming tail-latency and queue buildup. PID: alert-1798765432.

Anya Patel: seeing this in the dashboard, streaming token cadence collapsed around 12:34 UTC. KV cache size for model-x has grown ~6x in the last 10m.

Miguel Alvarez: confirmed. Continuous-batching worker queues are accumulating; partial flushes not happening. Looks like some requests are pinning KV pages.

Jia Chen: any recent deploys?

Deploy Bot: Deploy event: runtime-service:release-2026.04.11-a at 12:20 UTC by jenkins-bot. Change: adjust continuous_batch_window from 6ms -> 20ms (canary on 10% -> went to 100% at 12:22).

Sophia Li: that matches. 20ms window could amplify batching and increase live KV cache retention. Hypothesis: batch window increase + new cache key prefix change => scanning more prefixes and preventing normal eviction.

Anya Patel: we should roll back the batch-window change ASAP and temporarily disable continuous batching for model-x to stop cache blowup.

Miguel Alvarez: I can push a hotfix. Plan: 1) set continuous_batch_enabled=false via FF; 2) revert batch_window to 6ms; 3) increase cache-eviction frequency to 30s; 4) restart streaming workers gradually.

Jia Chen: callout — rolling restart will cause short reconnects for streaming clients. CS Triage, heads-up for affected customers.

CS Triage: copying customer-impact list from logs now. So far: 3 enterprise customers (acct A, acct B, acct C) showing degraded responses and reconnects. No widespread error codes yet but high latency/timeouts for long-tail streams.

Miguel Alvarez: executing hotfix steps. First toggling feature flag.

Miguel Alvarez: ```
# toggle FF to disable continuous batching for model-x
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"continuous_batching_model_x","value":false}' \
  https://flags.redwood.example/api/v1/flags
```

Deploy Bot: Feature flag update acknowledged. change-id ff-8721.

Anya Patel: patching config to revert batch_window. Applying via configmap to runtime-service-3.

Miguel Alvarez: ```
# kube rollout of configmap
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-service-config
data:
  continuous_batch_window: "6"
  cache_eviction_interval_secs: "30"
EOF
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-service-3
```

SRE Rotation: restarting workers with 30s stagger to avoid herd reconnections.

Jia Chen: monitoring memory and latency. Please post metrics.

Miguel Alvarez: memory usage dropping on nodes node-gpu-1/2; KV cache size for model-x reduced from 420GB -> 140GB within 6 minutes. Latency p95 down to ~300ms.

Sophia Li: partial flush counter shows flushes resumed after FF flip. Looks like new batching path was skipping partial flush on stale page boundary. Root cause likely a regression in batching flush condition introduced in release-2026.04.11-a.

Anya Patel: creating short-lived rollback release to pin continuous batching to old behavior. Also opening a postmortem issue and assigning to eng-runtime.

CS Triage: customers A/B/C notified via status page about degraded streaming for ~20m and mitigations in progress. No data exfiltration, only performance/reconnects.

Deploy Bot: Incident severity set to P2 due to multiple paying customers impacted and potential OOM risk. Pager duty acknowledged by Miguel and Anya.

Miguel Alvarez: I'll keep the FF off for model-x until the fix lands in canary and validated. Next steps for eng-runtime: reproduce the partial flush scenario locally, add unit test for boundary condition, and add a guard to avoid scanning > N prefixes in one tick.

Jia Chen: saving dumps of KV metadata and sample requests to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1798765432/ for postmortem.

Sophia Li: quick mitigation note for prod runbook: if KV cache growth > 200% in 5m, toggle continuous_batching for affected model and raise eviction frequency. We'll add a short alert for that.

Anya Patel: handoff to next on-call (SRE Rotation) at 13:00 UTC. Handoff summary: hotfix applied (FF disabled, batch_window reverted), cache size reduced, p95 improved, customers notified, root cause likely batching flush regression in release-2026.04.11-a, investigation ongoing. Logs and dumps uploaded.

SRE Rotation: taking over. I'll watch for reoccurrence and coordinate with eng-runtime for hotfix release. Please post any TOD (things of documentation) or follow-ups.

Miguel Alvarez: follow-up tickets: ENG-RUNTIME-1127 (partial flush regression), ENG-RUNTIME-1128 (add KV growth alert), ENG-OPS-231 (playbook update).

CS Triage: will keep customers updated and post incident summary when we have postmortem.

Anya Patel: thanks team. Marking this thread 'incident-in-progress' until postmortem is published. :white_check_mark:
